info.text:
Only 24% of surveyed Americans had a will in 2025. Without one, state law has a default plan.

Dying without a will is called intestacy, and the rules vary by state.
In New York, a spouse with kids gets the first $50,000 plus half the rest. On a $250,000 estate (hypothetical), that's $150,000 to the spouse and $100,000 to the kids.
Unmarried partners get $0 under New York's intestacy law. Under the Uniform Probate Code, with no relatives, the estate goes to the state.

Sources: Caring.com Wills and Estate Planning Study (2022-2025); NY EPTL 4-1.1; Uniform Probate Code 2-102, 2-105.
News and education, not financial advice. Not legal advice.
